MRP basics:
- Take in survey data 
- Multilevel regression: Run regression predicting outcome based on binned geographic+ demographic characteristics (forming "cells" of specific permutations of said info). Random effects enable partial pooling to draw on info of related cells
- Postratification: use ACS data to model amount of that cell in a given geographic area, producing a (hopefully accurate) mapping

Notes:

- Remember variable names must match exactly between postrat frame and input data
- Shiro data built for CCES. Need to build similar pipelines, general idea is get data to match, then run it through models. Plenty of models on the MRP end, just need to pick best one for purposes

# Synthetic Joint: Smoothfix vs Bmlogit
## Methodological difference:
- Smoothfix (iterative proportional fitting): Takes ACS demographic frame, rakes uniformly to hit CCES partisan marginals by state. Assumes demographic × partisan independence within raking.
- Bmlogit (multinomial with balancing constraints): Fits multinomial model on survey data to learn demographic to partisan relationships, then reweights to hit CCES marginals. Preserves survey covariance structure.

## Results
- Cell-level correlation: r = 0.992
- State partisan marginal correlation with CCES: ~0.978 (bmlogit)
- Either is basically fine!

- Income essentially irrelevant
